title: Reduced Sensory Attenuation Scales with Tic Severity in Tourette Syndrome
evidence_type: peer-reviewed primary cross-sectional behavioral case-control study; abstract-only extraction
date_caveat: Publication is dated October 28; no within-day UTC time verified. PubMed/Entrez timestamps lack verified timezone. New to prior search and repository, not proof of exact post-cutoff ordering.
population: Thirty adults with Tourette syndrome and 30 healthy controls; severe persistent subgroup not separately established.
exposure: Force matching using direct finger reproduction versus indirect button control.
outcomes: Behavioral sensory attenuation and contemporaneous YGTSS total tic severity.
results: TS group showed less force overestimation in the direct task; no group difference in indirect task. Reduced attenuation associated with greater current tic severity beyond medication load, obsessive-compulsive symptoms and premonitory urges.
precision: Numeric effect estimates, uncertainty, model denominator, missingness, interaction test and out-of-sample performance not in verified abstract.
negative_findings: Indirect-condition group null retained. Direct significance and indirect nonsignificance do not establish a formal group-by-condition interaction.
claim_supported: Task-specific adult sensorimotor association worth primary-methods follow-up.
claim_not_supported: Causation, universal trigger, prospectively validated biomarker, treatment efficacy or diagnostic test. Authors first-direct-evidence wording is not independently established novelty.
risk_of_bias: No calibration or prospective prediction established
adverse_events: No treatment tested; no clinical safety estimate.
cohort_overlap: No overlap with older paired-air-puff gating study established; distinct paradigms must not be pooled as the same endpoint.
access: Official PubMed API abstract inspected transiently; web-reader PubMed inaccessible. No source body or participant data retained.
correction_retraction_check: No linked notice in current PubMed metadata.
next_verification_task: Lawful full methods/table retrieval for exact group-by-condition analysis, uncertainty, medication handling, model n and independent validation; no participant request or clinical action.
